races.name: MJG Group Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Pull The Rug
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Grace Harris with a moderate sim-going record (1 win from 8), Rossa Ryan holds the ride but this horse's best form has come on good ground and the wide back draw gives little positional advantage in a race where closers need things to go right.

runners_data.name: Bold Shout
runners_data.note: Prominent-style three-year-old from Clive Cox's yard with a recent win at 6f on good ground and a placed run in soft, giving genuine soft-ground confidence; Hector Crouch is well placed to deliver a well-timed challenge from just behind the leaders.

runners_data.name: Black Endeavour
runners_data.note: Midfield runner who landed a 6f win on good ground earlier in the form string and showed a placed effort on soft, though Callum Rodriguez's mount has been in action just 8 days ago and the trainer's 14-day record of 0 wins from 6 is a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Maid In Devon
runners_data.note: Front-runner with three wins from her last five starts including victories at 6f on good and on soft, giving her standout claims in this race shape; Lewis Edmunds partners a filly whose bold-jumping style from stall 10 suits the contested pace scenario perfectly.

runners_data.name: Jenny Jerome
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who steps up to 6f having run best over 5f, and her form string includes a placed run in soft but connections' 14-day record of 0 from 4 suggests the stable is not in its sharpest vein; the wide draw in stall 11 may not help.

runners_data.name: Red Snapper
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has won back-to-back races at 6f on good ground and showed a placed effort at 5f in a similar context, making her the most credible late-closer in the field; Ben Ffrench Davis (5lb claimer) rides from stall 9, and blinkers are noted as headgear.

runners_data.name: Nebbia
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's three-year-old holds genuinely strong hold-up instincts, but with multiple closers in this field she is unlikely to secure her natural wide-berth position at the very rear; her recent form shows two fifth-place finishes at 6f, and the style-fit discount tempers her chance here.

runners_data.name: Eightthreeone
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner from Eve Johnson Houghton's yard who will battle Maid In Devon for the early lead from stall 6; her recent form shows consistent mid-pack finishes at 6f on good ground, and if the contested pace burns her out she may not have enough left late.

runners_data.name: White Ladder
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after a 60-day absence for John Ryan, with placed form over 7f on soft suggesting stamina, but stepping back to 6f and needing things to happen in front of him makes this a tricky race to win from his usual position.

runners_data.name: Mollstar
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for Ed Walker who ran a solid second at 6f on good ground most recently; George Downing takes the ride and the trainer's excellent 14-day strike rate (6 wins from 42) is worth noting as a stable-in-form flag.

runners_data.name: Guernsey Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent type from David Evans's yard who has struggled for a win recently but showed a placed run at 6f on good-to-soft; Pat Cosgrave rides from stall 12 and the soft conditions are within her range, though the form string has drifted towards mid-pack finishes.

runners_data.name: Pilgrim's Progress
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon-trained prominent runner with multiple placed efforts at 5-6f, including runner-up finishes on standard track and fibresand; Alec Voikhansky partners from stall 3 and while the trip suits, the horse has not yet won and the soft ground is untested for her.

runners_data.name: Madman
runners_data.note: Prominent-style racer for the Cook & Bridger partnership who has won twice at 6f on good ground and placed in soft, making him the highest-OR runner in the field; Jack Callan rides from stall 13 and four placed runs from 15 starts in similar ground underline that this trip and conditions genuinely suit.

races.paceDynamic: Maid In Devon and Eightthreeone are both confirmed front-runners drawn in stalls 10 and 6 respectively, meaning they will lock horns from the off on this 6f Salisbury straight and ensure a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a dawdle. The soft ground will place a premium on stamina and jumping clear of trouble, and with the pace distributed across the early splits, the race is unlikely to be a muddling affair — those who can sustain their effort through the home straight from a handy position will be best placed. Madman and Bold Shout, both prominent types, will look to slot in behind the pace-setters, adding further pressure to the front rank, while the hold-up brigade at the back — Red Snapper, Pull The Rug, White Ladder — will need a strong enough gallop to close, which this shape should provide. The field holds more hold-up types than can all get a genuinely clear run from the rear, with Nebbia in particular unlikely to secure its natural position at the back given the number of runners mapped there; the tactical verdict favours prominent-to-lead profiles who can dictate or track the speed and sustain their run through testing ground, rather than those relying on a single late surge from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Leaders Dominant
scenarios.trigger: If Maid In Devon and Eightthreeone set a genuine contested gallop that strings the field out, the horse who can control the tempo or track just off it wins.
scenarios.body: The honest early pace on soft ground suits a horse who either leads with authority or sits a length off the speed, as the sustained gallop will exhaust those who chase hard and advantage those racing within themselves near the front; Maid In Devon's recent winning form at 6f on similar ground marks her as the most likely beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners press each other into the ground and a prominent type conserves energy just off the pace to pounce in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Bold Shout arrives with strong recent form including a win at 6f on good ground and Hector Crouch knows how to deliver at the death; Madman's hat-trick form and soft-ground place record give him an equally compelling claims to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Closes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is extreme enough to create a significant gap that allows genuine closers to sweep through on the wide outside in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Red Snapper has back-to-back wins at 6f and a hold-up style that would thrive if the race truly burns along, while Pull The Rug showed a placed effort on similar going; however, this scenario is partly dependent on Nebbia, whose redistribution from the back of the field means it may not get the clean trip it needs from its true style.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Chaos Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground deteriorates handling across runners and the race breaks up into a fragmented, slow-motion scramble with several horses underperforming.
scenarios.body: Black Endeavour's placed soft-ground form and Guernsey Angel's placed run at 6f on good-to-soft could see unconsidered types creep into contention if the expected shape simply doesn't materialise; this remains a low-probability outcome given the confirmed pace presence at the head of affairs.

watchPoints.text: Maid In Devon and Eightthreeone will fight for the early lead — watch whether Maid In Devon asserts control by the 2f mark or is forced to use extra energy matching Eightthreeone, as that battle will dictate how much she has left for the finish.

Madman is the highest-OR runner in the race and arrives on the back of back-to-back wins; if Jack Callan can secure a prominent position just off the front pair from stall 13, he becomes the most dangerous single challenger in the field.

Nebbia is mapped to midfield but is a genuine hold-up type — if she is caught wider or further forward than ideal in a congested 13-runner field, her chance is materially compromised and she should be downgraded in running.

Red Snapper carries blinkers and is the standout closer in the race — watch the first two furlongs to see if the pace is truly strong enough to create the gap she needs, as on soft ground with horses tiring early, she could be the biggest mover in the final furlong.
Mollstar's trainer Ed Walker has six wins from 42 runners in the past 14 days — an unusually sharp form line for this yard — making this runner worth monitoring in the market for any late confidence.

races.name: PKF Francis Clark Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tenbob Tommy
runners_data.note: Won twice at 6f on Good ground but his two similar-going runs return 0 wins and 0 places, and at 5 years old on soft for the first time he faces an unproven stamina test at this trip; prominent style means he'll be caught in the early scrimmage for position.

runners_data.name: Sergeant Pep
runners_data.note: Clive Cox in decent 14-day form (2/20) and Rossa Ryan in the saddle is an upgrade; has placed on soft at 6f and consistent recent form (2-3-2-3) makes him the steadiest of the prominent horses and the most credible danger to Supreme King.

runners_data.name: Supreme King
runners_data.note: Strand top selection at medium confidence — has a win and a place from 15 soft-going runs and his midfield style suits a race where the front group will burn energy early; Pat Cosgrave partners a horse who has recorded a 6f win at this course level and knows how to switch off.

runners_data.name: Rare Change
runners_data.note: Headgear (p) worn, hold-up style, and a win on soft (1/7f/SOF) in his history, but six of his last seven runs have returned finishes of 7th or worse; Richard Hughes had two wins from 29 runs over 14 days and the horse's inconsistency is a significant concern.

runners_data.name: The Quiet Gent
runners_data.note: Returning from 35 days off — the longest layoff in the field — and wears headgear (p); placed twice at 6f on Good and has soft-going form, but his trainer's 14-day record (0/3) is poor and the layoff adds doubt about his readiness.

runners_data.name: Baldomero
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old veteran wearing a hood (b), has placed at 6f on Good but 0 wins and 0 places from 15 soft-going runs is a red flag; Michael Appleby in good 14-day form (3/26) but the horse's age and going record undermine confidence.

runners_data.name: Padua
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, stepping back from 7f to 6f which may sharpen him, but has only one run on soft from four attempts and a tongue-tie is worn; Hector Crouch will need to control the tempo carefully to avoid being caught out by the prominent cluster behind him.

runners_data.name: Safari Dream
runners_data.note: Arrives on the back of consecutive 6f wins on Good ground and is the form horse in the race, but all his wins come on Good or better and the soft going is an untested variable that could blunt his early speed and finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Under The Twilight
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on Good (1/6f/GOO) and placed in similar conditions, but 0 wins and 0 places from four soft-going starts is a clear going concern; hold-up style means he depends on a strong pace to get competitive, which may not materialise with only Padua setting the fractions.

races.paceDynamic: Padua is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse wanting to lead, is likely to dictate at a controlled tempo on Good to Soft ground — a pace that will be measured rather than scorching. Four horses (Tenbob Tommy, Sergeant Pep, Baldomero, Safari Dream) want prominent positions and will jostle for that territory in the opening two furlongs, creating a crowded early contest that could cause interference and positional shuffling two to three furlongs out. Supreme King, operating from midfield, and the hold-up trio of Rare Change, The Quiet Gent and Under The Twilight will be tracking that prominent group, hoping Padua's controlled lead creates enough pace to allow their finishing efforts to land. The sustainable tempo on a softish surface over 6f suits patient midfield-to-hold-up runners who can pick up through a tiring pack — this race shape broadly favours a horse travelling smoothly in the slipstream and hitting the line late, giving the midfield and hold-up profiles an edge, though the prominent runners will be close enough to capitalise if the pace collapses entirely in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Padua Dictates, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Padua sets a controlled, even gallop and the prominent scrimmage wastes energy early, leaving the field to unwind in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Padua's lone lead at a sustainable tempo means those who travel off the pace conserve energy for a late surge, with the soft ground stretching stamina and rewarding horses that finish strongly; Supreme King, coming from midfield on a course where he has winning form, is ideally positioned to pick off rivals in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble Pays Off
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent horses fight for position early and the pace quickens enough to string out the field, suiting one who settles just behind Padua.
scenarios.body: One of the prominent horses secures a clean position and benefits from a clear run on the rail or wide, outpacing rivals who are hampered by traffic in the congested 2-3f section; Sergeant Pep, in consistent placed form on soft and with Rossa Ryan steering, is the likeliest to navigate this and arrive late enough to outsprint.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo lifts through the middle stages and the prominent horses overcook it, leaving a clear late-running lane for a closer.
scenarios.body: Rare Change and The Quiet Gent, both wearing headgear and carrying hold-up profiles, would benefit from a strung-out field where they can weave through tired rivals; both have winning form on soft but their recent 7-rated finishes suggest they need everything to go right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Safari Dream Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Safari Dream — in flying form with back-to-back wins — bounces out and challenges Padua's lead, converting to a pace-pressing display.
scenarios.body: Safari Dream arrives on a hat-trick bid and would only win if Padua fades quickly and the other prominent types fail to match his early stride, but his Good ground wins suggest soft may blunt his sharpness; the scenario is possible but relies on conditions that don't currently align with his profile.

watchPoints.text: Watch the prominent cluster of Tenbob Tommy, Sergeant Pep, Baldomero and Safari Dream between 2f and 3f out — four horses chasing one spot behind Padua creates a real traffic flashpoint where interference is likely.

Padua's solo lead may be deceptively slow — if Hector Crouch takes a very conservative approach, the pack could bunch behind him, turning this into a sprint finish that negates hold-up horses entirely.

Safari Dream's going suitability is the key unknown; if he fails to quicken on soft, the recent back-to-back wins on Good will have flattered his current form profile and punters backing him on that run of form may be caught out.

Under The Twilight has a 0-from-4 record on soft going — if conditions come up genuinely testing rather than riding Good to Soft as described, his participation in the finish becomes increasingly unlikely despite his strong Good-ground profile.

Supreme King's draw in stall 8 places him wide but his midfield style means he'll be angled inward naturally — Pat Cosgrave should find a clean passage once the prominent battle resolves in the first 2f.

races.name: Happy 40th Birthday Kevin Baker Selling Stakes

runners_data.name: Persian Land
runners_data.note: Has won on soft and placed on similar ground — the most relevant soft-going profile in the field; midfield style suits the anticipated pace collapse over 7f and Callum Rodriguez's recent form for David Evans (2 from 23 in 14 days) keeps confidence measured rather than high.

runners_data.name: Absolute Diamond
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 7f trip on soft at her most recent start, giving her the most directly relevant recent form in the race; Pat Cosgrave adds experience, though her midfield style means she needs the pace to be genuine.

runners_data.name: Hello You Ten
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner who is flagged as a fader in the finish — likely to force the early pace alongside Minzaal Time but is doing everyone else a favour by doing so; tongue-tie adds a small unknown.

runners_data.name: Minzaal Time
runners_data.note: Co-pace-setter who fades late and has shown little consistency across five starts, mostly on Tapeta and Good; the blinkered headgear may sharpen his early effort but the fade pattern on soft ground over 7f is a significant concern.

runners_data.name: Courage Best
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile on Good ground with zero places from five starts on soft-ish conditions; ran just four days ago, which is a stamina and freshness flag, and his modest soft-going record (0 wins, 0 places in similar conditions) gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Oxber Flyer
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed with no handicap rating to assess; going preference and style are unknown quantities, making any assessment speculative, though trainer Charlie Clover's modest 14-day strike rate (2 from 4) provides little confidence around a debut or early run.

runners_data.name: Our Fella
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent, regularly finishing placed in 5f-6f company but now steps up to 7f for the first time; the fade flag in the finish and the step in trip are risks, though the claim of 7lb from Isobelle Chalmers may help in a competitive but modest selling contest.

runners_data.name: Lushill
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with genuine 7f experience, including a placed run over the trip on Good, and looks one of the likelier horses to secure a forward position when the field sorts itself; William Cox's stable (J S Moore) is on a reasonable run of form.

runners_data.name: The Kalonji Man
runners_data.note: Races naturally in midfield but is mapped to the rear because true hold-up types are scarce in this field — his actual running style means he will not sit as deep as the redistribution suggests; soft-ground profile is moderate at best (0 wins, 0 places) and the Richard Hannon booking with a modest low OR of 45 gives limited grounds for confidence.

runners_data.name: Grapple
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just one start (12th of field on Good over 7f) and blinkered today — Ralph Beckett's 9 from 45 in 14 days shows stable form but the horse is deeply unexposed and has shown nothing on its only outing; the 56-day break is also a concern.

races.paceDynamic: Minzaal Time and Hello You Ten are confirmed front-runners and will fight for control from the gates, creating a genuinely contested early pace on Good To Soft ground over 7f at Salisbury — an honest gallop is the baseline expectation. Both are flagged as faders in the finish, meaning the lead is likely to be surrendered in the closing stages, handing a tactical advantage to horses able to track the pace from just off it and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs. This race shape squarely favours prominent racers or medium-pace horses with proven soft-ground stamina who can sit within striking distance and pick up the pieces. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position; of the prominent horses, Lushill and Our Fella are best placed to actually land a forward berth, with Our Fella the likelier to get outpaced for position given the draw and competition.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Minzaal Time and Hello You Ten burn each other out through a contested early gallop and capitulate in the straight, allowing mid-to-rear trackers to sweep through.
scenarios.body: The two lead faders set a hot tempo that they cannot sustain on soft ground over 7f, leaving the race wide open for horses able to travel through the early stages and finish strongly; Good To Soft conditions favour those who conserve early energy and sustain into the home straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners establishes a clear advantage unchallenged and the pace becomes controlled and even, allowing a prominent tracker to travel comfortably and win doing less.
scenarios.body: If Hello You Ten or Minzaal Time settles into a rhythm rather than fighting hard for the lead, a prominent runner like Lushill can sit just off the pace and pounce before the fade fully sets in; Lushill's 7f experience and proximity to the pace make this a credible alternative.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Sweeper Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and consistent, allowing a midfield horse with proven soft-ground ability to close powerfully from off the pace in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Persian Land, with a win on soft over 6f and a placed run on similar ground, is ideally suited to coming from the middle of the pack in a truly-run 7f race; Absolute Diamond's course-like form adds a secondary threat from a similar position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises on Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace fragments the field and creates a messy, strung-out race that opens gaps for a lightly-raced or unexposed type to grab a minor position unchallenged.
scenarios.body: Oxber Flyer is completely unexposed and could find soft ground and an honest pace suiting a debut or lightly-raced profile; Grapple, similarly lightly raced, cannot be entirely dismissed though both face significant unknowns.

watchPoints.text: Minzaal Time and Hello You Ten — if they fight hard for the lead from the outset, monitor whether either capitulates before the 2f pole; a premature fade by both would validate the pace-collapse scenario.

Persian Land — drawn 8 in a 10-runner field, watch whether Callum Rodriguez can get the horse into a good tracking position early; if trapped wide or too far back, the 7f trip on soft becomes a stern test.

Lushill — drawn 10 on the outside and prominent in style; watch whether William Cox can slot into a forward position without expending too much energy in the first furlong, as a wide trip around Salisbury's track could cost ground.
Oxber Flyer — completely unknown quantity; any show of early pace or prominent positioning in the first 2f should be noted as an indicator of whether it can factor in the finish.

Our Fella — the step up from 5f-6f to 7f is the critical watch point; if she drops out of contention before the 3f pole, the trip has found her out, but if she holds her prominent position into the straight, the Chalmers claim makes her competitively weighted.

runners_data.name: Soul Icon
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old prominent racer in good form on good ground but showing 0W0P on similar going; Josephine Gordon takes over and the soft conditions are a question mark, though the strong early pace from three front-runners suits a horse who can travel prominently without leading — 20 days since last run is fine.

runners_data.name: Quickthorn
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with one recent soft-ground run (5th/16f/Soft) suggesting he handles the going; at OR 108 he is outclassed on ratings but will force the pace regardless, and the burning question is whether he merely sets it up for others before tiring badly in the straight.

runners_data.name: Lion's Pride
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse by style returning from a 133-day absence, stepping up sharply from 12f to 14f+ with a hat-trick at 12f on good ground last season; Robert Havlin and the Gosden yard are capable of placing a fresh horse well, and this race shape — a hard pace likely to collapse — is precisely what Lion's Pride's profile needs.

runners_data.name: Amiloc
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection is a confirmed front-runner whose recent form is poor — 7th on soft, unseated, two 6ths — but Ralph Beckett's stable (T14: 9/45) is in decent nick; Rossa Ryan may try to steal a march early, though whether Amiloc can hold off Quickthorn and Nightime Dancer in a three-way lead battle at OR 114 is the critical uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Nightime Dancer
runners_data.note: At OR 93 the lowest-rated runner and a front-runner by nature, returning after 41 days with headgear (blinkers) noted; form figures of 0 and 7 and 14 in recent starts suggest he is likely to set pace for others before fading, and Richard Hannon's T14 strike rate (2/47) does not inspire confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Amiloc, Quickthorn, and Nightime Dancer are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a contested, pressured gallop from the outset over 1m6f on Good to Soft ground at Salisbury. With three horses fighting for the lead, the pace will be genuine and sustained — none can afford to yield and then work back into contention at this trip, meaning the early fractions will be honest and the race will be run as a true test of stamina. This strong gallop is expected to string the field out and drain the finishing kick of those involved in the early battle, leaving the door open for a horse that can track the pace without burning energy needlessly in the vanguard. This race shape firmly favours a prominent-to-midfield runner who can travel smoothly behind a fast early pace and produce a measured late effort — Soul Icon and Lion's Pride are the profiles that stand to gain most from the carnage up front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Battle, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners fight hard for position early and the pace remains brutal throughout, grinding rivals into submission
scenarios.body: Amiloc, Quickthorn, and Nightime Dancer burn each other out over the first mile, leaving whoever handles the pace best to sustain it longest; a horse with genuine stamina and the ability to handle soft ground at this trip will outlast exhausted rivals. Soul Icon, travelling prominently but not burning energy leading, is positioned to capitalise as the pace-setters tire in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners genuinely collapse in the straight after a fierce pace duel, allowing a hold-up horse to power through beaten rivals
scenarios.body: Lion's Pride, held up by Robert Havlin, is the natural beneficiary if the pace is truly suicidal — stepping up markedly in trip from 12f and returning after a 133-day absence, the Gosden yard will have him fresh and primed to finish strongly. The hold-up style is a perfect tactical fit for a race with three genuine lead horses, though the long absence and trip step-up are real unknowns.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Amiloc breaks cleanly under Rossa Ryan and establishes a comfortable lead while Quickthorn and Nightime Dancer are outpaced or checked early
scenarios.body: Amiloc dictating a controlled but honest pace removes the destructive speed duel element, allowing him to conserve energy and hold on into the soft ground; the Strand Scorecard flags him as top selection and Rossa Ryan's tactical awareness could be decisive if he seizes the rail early. However, Amiloc's recent form (7th on soft, U fall, 6th) is unconvincing and confidence here is appropriately low.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If none of the front-runners dominates cleanly, the pace becomes uneven and a rough-and-tumble affair produces an unexpected result
scenarios.body: An uncharacteristically messy race over 1m6f on soft ground could see any of the five runners involved at a critical point, but Nightime Dancer — lowest rated and least exposed at this trip — could benefit from chaos if the race falls apart tactically. This is the least likely outcome given the strong front-running intent across three runners.

watchPoints.text: Amiloc, Quickthorn, and Nightime Dancer are all intent on leading — watch the first two furlongs to see who breaks fastest and whether one horse gains a clear lead or all three fight destructively, as that determines whether Scenario A or C plays out.

Lion's Pride is returning from 133 days off and stepping up significantly in trip — watch the paddock and early movement to assess freshness; if he travels smoothly early, the hold-up profile is perfectly suited to this pace shape.

Soul Icon has no wins or places in similar soft conditions (0W0P from 2 runs) — if the going deteriorates further from Good to Soft, watch whether she handles the ground as the race develops or gets bogged down in the straight.

Nightime Dancer's blinkers are worth monitoring — first-time or re-applied headgear can produce an early bolt for the lead that exaggerates the pace even beyond what is expected, which could prove significant for the stamina test faced by all runners.

races.paceDynamic: Four confirmed front-runners — Fanciulla Del West, Next Guilian, Relentless Hero, and Takeitorleaveit — will contest the lead from the outset over 1m2f on soft ground at Salisbury, making a strong, sustained gallop virtually inevitable. Relentless Hero and Fanciulla Del West are both flagged as prominent-to-lead types who fade late, meaning their influence is likely to be felt early and then dissipate; Takeitorleaveit, despite sharing the lead profile, has a superior record of placing and winning and may be better equipped to regulate pace from a tactical position rather than burning fuel. The field holds more front-running types than can all occupy the early positions — Gatlinburg is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is crowded with similar types, and its true late-running style means it is racing into a shape that doesn't suit it. On soft ground over this trip, a genuinely contested early gallop will drain the field and favour a confirmed stayer with the tactical nous to settle just off the pace — the prominent-to-midfield profile that can switch off and sustain into the final two furlongs is the winning profile here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Stayer
scenarios.trigger: If the four lead types battle for supremacy and the soft ground compounds fatigue, creating a truly searching gallop that rewards a horse who settles and sustains.
scenarios.body: The early leaders drain each other's reserves on the Salisbury climb, and the winner is a horse who has been covered up in the first half and arrives with a genuine late run over this stamina-testing trip; soft ground accelerates the attrition.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Moderate Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Takeitorleaveit takes control and sets a measured gallop, allowing at least one of the lead types to last home in conditions that don't become truly gruelling.
scenarios.body: A steadier tempo means the leaders' stamina weaknesses are less exposed, and a horse with tactical speed and a decent OR can hold on into the placing positions without the race turning into a stamina slog.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Delivery Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce early and a genuine midfield tracker produces a well-timed run around the home turn to collar weakening leaders.
scenarios.body: A horse settled in midfield, not needing to battle for early position, tracks the strong pace and delivers the decisive challenge between the two-furlong marker and the finish on a track where the run-in rewards sustained galloping; soft going does not undermine this profile here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is extreme and the whole field stretches out, theoretically opening a gap for a pure hold-up horse finishing from the rear.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends partly on Gatlinburg, a genuine hold-up type racing out of its natural position due to field congestion at the rear, which materially reduces its execution likelihood; even if the pace scenario is right, the redistribution discount means this shape is the least reliable of the four.

watchPoints.text: Fanciulla Del West and Relentless Hero are both front-runners flagged as faders — if they push each other hard from the start on soft ground, both could collapse rapidly in the final two furlongs, dramatically opening the race for those behind.

Gatlinburg's 105-day absence combined with its redistribution out of its natural hold-up position means it faces a double handicap today — watch to see if it can find clear daylight late or whether field traffic negates its finishing kick entirely.

Takeitorleaveit is unproven on soft ground; if the going proves genuinely testing rather than the Good to Soft recorded elsewhere on the card, its consistent placing form on quicker surfaces must be treated with more caution than the Strand Scorecard's top rating implies.

Next Guilian has run exclusively at 8f in all recent starts — the step to 10f on soft is an untested combination, and if it sets or shares the early pace, it may ensure the gallop is strong enough to bring stamina into play more than connections would like.
